opening.argument: The video identifies itself as a live scambaiting activity, and the speaker expressly describes it as “a tech support person scambaiting tech support scammers.” The warning page, remote-access prompt, screen-viewing instruction, and claimed charge appear within that tested interaction with purported support callers, rather than as requests made by the creator to viewers. The displayed warning directs a computer user to call support, while the caller instructs the user to run GoToAssist and says they “will be able to see your screen.” The caller also claims a $5000 charge and requests the bank’s customer-care number. But the available evidence does not establish who operated the warning, whether access was granted, or whether any charge, payment, or data transfer occurred.
